For the horse clueless, why is it bad to ride without a saddle?

It's okay to ride bareback during light riding if you're a normal sized person. A saddle helps distribute the weight more evenly and reduces the impact on the horses back. Especially for jumping, sinking your weight into the stirrups greatly reduces the impact you have on the horse during landing.

Agree with saddles helping with weight distribution, but I disagree with sinking weight into the stirrups. When I first began eventing, my instructors had me practicing jumping without stirrups so I could learn to hold with my legs and gain the strength to do so without squeezing or losing balance.
The reason being that stirrups connect at the bars on the saddle and rather than distributing, all of your weight will pull down on those two points rather than across the back. Learning to hold with your legs took all the pressure off the spine.
Also learned to land in half-seat so my weight never "hits" the horse's back to begin with (though with the way you were taught, that wouldn't be an issue anyway. I hate when you see riders slamming down).

not trying to argue: just saying what I was taught and why.

Edit to add: I had one horse I used to jump bareback and bridless. Learning to hold with the legs kept me from slamming on his back jumping because I was used to it with no stirrups and landing in half-seat anyway. He never showed any signs of pain or discomfort doing that. But I do think if someone doesn't have the strength to hold themselves off the spine for jumping that they should absolutely not jump bareback and work over lower fences until they master the technique with a saddle.

Agreed. Bareback jumping is only for advanced riders. This ham is clearly far from being advanced! It kills me too when I see a rider slamming down on a horse's back, I've seen it happen with people riding swayback horses too. Just terrible.
